Bitcoin (BTC) broke local resistance to trade between $65,500 and $65,800 on June 15, 2026, catalyzed by a surprise U.S.-Iran peace agreement that triggered a broad risk-on rally across global markets. This geopolitical de-escalation snapped a five-day streak of spot Bitcoin ETF outflows, returning positive inflows to major funds. Simultaneously, industry pressure is mounting on U.S. Senate leadership to schedule a floor vote for the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act before the summer recess, aiming to formalize SEC and CFTC jurisdictions.

Meanwhile, macro allocators remain highly focused on the June 16–17 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, the first led by newly confirmed Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh. With U.S. annual inflation climbing to 4.2% in May, markets anticipate a hawkish policy stance, holding rates at 3.50%–3.75%. Yields on the U.S. 10-year Treasury note are hovering near cycle highs, while the S&P 500 registers minor gains. A stronger U.S. dollar continues to compress non-yielding digital asset valuations, maintaining a tight inverse correlation between DXY and Bitcoin.
